title: Distilling Bidirectional Embedding Teachers into Streaming-Compatible Causal Students

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to provide streaming-compatible text embeddings (KV-cache reusable) without sacrificing the quality of bidirectional attention. None of the prior papers explicitly address this objective. While papers like [10], [12], [13], and [14] discuss KV-cache reuse, they focus on accelerating inference or enabling multi-tenant systems rather than embedding quality or compatibility with bidirectional attention. Similarly, papers like [5] and [26] discuss embedding quality and distillation but do not address streaming compatibility or KV-cache reuse. Thus, no prior paper shares the same purpose.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves a teacher-student distillation framework that trains a bidirectional teacher with GG-SM (Gradient-Guided Soft Masking) and distills it into a causal student using a combination of InfoNCE contrastive loss and MSE distillation loss. Papers [5], [8], [18], and [23] discuss knowledge distillation frameworks for embeddings or language models, and [8] specifically mentions contrastive representation distillation. However, none of these papers combine GG-SM with InfoNCE and MSE loss in the same framework. GG-SM itself appears novel, as no prior paper mentions a similar masking mechanism. Therefore, the mechanism is not substantively equivalent to any prior work.

### Evaluation
The evaluation involves measuring the distilled student's performance on MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) and its streaming speedup via KV-cache reuse. Paper [31] introduces MTEB-NL, a benchmark for Dutch embeddings, which is part of the MTEB family. Papers [10], [12], [13], and [14] evaluate KV-cache reuse strategies, albeit for different tasks. Since the evaluation design reuses the MTEB benchmark family and measures KV-cache reuse, the evaluation facet is covered.

### Domain
The domain is text embeddings and streaming inference. Papers [5], [8], [9], [10], [12], [13], [14], and [16] all operate in the general area of text embeddings or streaming inference. While the specific focus on KV-cache reuse for streaming-compatible embeddings may be narrower, it falls within the broader domain of text embeddings and streaming inference. Thus, the domain is covered.

## Purpose: Provide streaming-compatible text embeddings (KV-cache reusable) without giving up the quality of bidirectional attention.

The core objective is closing the quality gap between causal (streaming-friendly) and bidirectional (quality-focused) text embeddings. Paper [10] discusses KV cache reuse for downstream tasks but focuses on sampling/reasoning, not text embeddings. Paper [30] compares bidirectional encoders vs. causal decoders for classification but doesn't address streaming compatibility or KV-cache reuse for embeddings. No prior paper specifically pursues the objective of making causal LM embeddings match bidirectional quality while preserving KV-cache reusability for streaming inference. The closest are [2] and [5] which do distillation for sentence embeddings, but their purpose is model compression (large→small), not causal→bidirectional quality recovery for streaming.

## Mechanism: Teacher-student distillation with GG-SM (Gradient-Guided Soft Masking) on the teacher + InfoNCE + MSE distillation loss on the student.

Paper [2] (DistillCSE) combines contrastive learning with knowledge distillation for sentence embeddings — InfoNCE-style contrastive loss + distillation loss combination is present. Paper [5] (DistilCSE) also applies knowledge distillation for contrastive sentence embeddings. Paper [8] (Contrastive Representation Distillation) uses contrastive objectives for distillation. However, the GG-SM (Gradient-Guided Soft Masking) component — using gradient signals to guide soft masking of the teacher's attention — is a specific primitive. Paper [28] covers differentiable soft-masked attention, but not gradient-guided masking for distillation purposes. Paper [23] uses masked inputs for distillation but with random masking (MAE-style), not gradient-guided. The combination of gradient-guided soft masking on the teacher side with InfoNCE+MSE on the student side appears not covered as a unified primitive. The InfoNCE+MSE combination for sentence embedding distillation is in [2] and [5], but GG-SM is not present.

## Evaluation: 68.1% gap-closure on MTEB + 4.1x streaming speedup via KV-cache reuse.

MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) is used as the evaluation benchmark. Paper [31] explicitly uses MTEB as an evaluation framework ("Massive Text Embedding Benchmark"). The gap-closure metric design (measuring how much a student closes the gap to teacher on MTEB) is a standard relative improvement metric on a named benchmark. The streaming speedup measurement is a standard throughput/latency metric. Both evaluation designs (MTEB-based quality evaluation + inference speedup measurement) appear in prior work at the design level — MTEB in [31], and speedup measurements are standard in distillation/efficiency papers like [1], [5].

## Domain: Text embeddings / streaming inference.

Paper [2] and [5] work in text/sentence embeddings. Paper [31] works explicitly in text embeddings (MTEB). Streaming inference for LLMs is addressed in [10], [12], [13], [14]. The combination of text embeddings + streaming is the specific sub-area, but both components exist in prior work. The domain of text embeddings is clearly covered by [2], [5], [31].
